discovery: Proposal and realization of spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Seigo Tarucha
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Japan

motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed encoding quantum information in the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot, with gates driven by electrically controlled exchange coupling. This proposal, together with DiVincenzo's criteria for a physical quantum computer, set out a concrete solid-state route to quantum information processing. Tarucha's pioneering work on few-electron quantum dots, which revealed shell structure and Hund's rules in artificial atoms, provided the experimental platform. His later development of micromagnet-based electric-dipole spin resonance enabled fast, high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gates in silicon, beyond fault-tolerance thresholds. Together these contributions turned the spin of a single electron, a textbook quantum object, into a controllable and scalable qubit. Single-spin readout, coherent control and entanglement in nanostructures are now established, and industrial-scale silicon spin-qubit processors are being built on CMOS-compatible technology.
